chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Durays al-Kunasi who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the testimony of people of a faith, whether it is valid for a man from outside their faith? He said: 'No, unless no one else is found in that situation; if no one else is found, their testimony is valid in the will, because it is not fitting that the right of a Muslim be lost, nor that his will be invalidated.'
ai.seo_question: When is the testimony of non-Muslims valid for Muslims in Islamic jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Baqir clarifies that while the testimony of *Ahl al-Milla* (people of a specific faith, often interpreted as non-Muslims or other sects) is generally invalid for Muslims, it becomes permissible under the principle of *idtirar* (necessity) when no Muslim witnesses are available. This ruling ensures the preservation of the deceased's rights and prevents the nullification of their will, reflecting the Shia juristic priority of maintaining legal continuity over strict adherence to witness criteria in cases of scarcity.
